We have template 101725 which converts phenol + carbonyl (maybe carbonate) to methyl ether. It seems to be O-methylation using methyl carbonate? The retro_smarts: [CH3]-[O]-[c] >> O-C(=O)-[CH3] + phenol. So forward reaction is phenol + methyl carbonate -> methyl ether + CO2? Not exactly but could be used for methoxy formation.

Thus we can use template 101725 for methoxy formation.

Now we have three templates: 101725 (methoxy formation), 6195 (SN2 substitution), 647549 (amide formation). Need to construct route JSON.

We need to define precursor molecules for each reaction.

Step3 (last step forward) would be methoxy formation: starting from phenol (c1cccc(NC(=O)... )c1) and methyl carbonate? But we can just list phenol and methyl iodide? However template expects O-C(=O)-[CH3] (methyl carbonate) as reactant. The retro_smarts shows product [CH3]-O-aryl formed from O-C(=O)-CH3 and phenol. So precursors: phenol (c1cccc(NC(=O)... )c1) and methyl carbonate (O=C(O)C). Methyl carbonate SMILES: COCO? Actually methyl carbonate is CO2CH3: O=C(O)C. SMILES: O=C(O)C. So we can use "O=C(O)C". Good.

Step2 SN2: we need aryl chloride precursor (aryl with Cl) and azetidine amine (N4CC(F)C4). The azetidine SMILES: N4CC(F)C4 is a four-membered ring with N and F. That's a secondary amine? The SMILES is N4CC(F)C4. We'll use that as nucleophile. The aryl chloride is the phenyl ring bearing the side chain (CH2-Ph) with Cl at benzylic position? Actually SN2 attaches azetidine to benzylic carbon attached to phenyl. The precursor could be "Cc3ccc(Cl)cc3" (chloromethyl phenyl). The side chain is Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3. So we need chloromethyl phenyl (ClCH2-Ph) and azetidine (N4CC(F)C4). So precursor SMILES: "ClCc3ccc(cc3)"? Actually chloromethyl phenyl: "ClCc1ccc(cc1)". Use "ClCc1ccc(cc1)". Good.

Step1 amide formation: precursors: 4-methoxyaniline (COc1cccc(NH2)c1) and triazine-5-carboxylic acid (c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N) with carboxylic acid? Actually need acyl chloride of triazine? Template 647549 uses O-[C](=O)-aryl + NH2-aryl -> amide. So we need acyl chloride? The retro_smarts shows O-[C](=O)-aryl + NH2-aryl -> amide. So reactants: acyl chloride (or acid?) O-[C](=O)-aryl is maybe acid chloride? Actually O-[C](=O)-aryl is an acyl chloride? O- attached to carbonyl? Might be acid chloride (Cl-C(=O)-aryl). But the SMILES shows O-[C;H0;D3;+0:1](=[O;D1;H0:2])-[c:3] which is an acyl chloride? O-? Not sure. But we can assume we need "ClC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N". That's acyl chloride of triazine. So precursor SMILES: "ClC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N". And 4-methoxyaniline: "COc1cccc(NH2)c1".

Thus route:

Root molecule target.

Children: reaction 1 (last step forward) maybe methoxy formation? The order in route is forward synthesis order: first reaction (closest to target) is amide formation? Actually we need 3 reactions applied sequentially to build target from starting materials. The root is target, children are reaction nodes that produce it from precursors. The order: first reaction (top) could be amide formation (makes target from anisidine and triazine acyl chloride). But we also need methoxy formation earlier to get anisidine from phenol. So order: Reaction A (amide formation) uses anisidine (which itself is product of methoxy formation) and triazine acyl chloride (which itself is product of SN2? Actually triazine acyl chloride already contains side chain with phenyl bearing azetidine; that side chain is built via SN2 earlier). So we have three steps:

Step3 (final) amide formation (template 647549) -> precursors: anisidine (product of methoxy step) and triazine acyl chloride (product of SN2 step).

Step2 (methoxy formation) (template 101725) -> precursors: phenol (c1cccc(NH2)c1) and methyl carbonate (O=C(O)C). This yields anisidine.

Step1 (SN2) (template 6195) -> precursors: chloromethyl phenyl (ClCH2-Ph) and azetidine (N4CC(F)C4) -> yields triazine acyl chloride? Wait SN2 attaches azetidine to phenyl side chain, but the triazine acyl chloride also includes that phenyl side chain attached to triazine. Actually the triazine acyl chloride is "ClC(=O)c2nnn(Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3)c2N". The side chain is attached to triazine via CH2 to phenyl bearing CN4... So SN2 step should produce the phenyl side chain with azetidine attached, which is part of the triazine acyl chloride. So the product of SN2 is "Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3" (the phenyl with side chain). Then that is attached to triazine via the carbonyl? Actually the triazine acyl chloride attaches to that phenyl via CH2? The triazine has substituent "Cc3ccc(CN4CC(F)C4)cc3". That's a benzyl group attached to triazine. So SN2 yields that benzyl phenyl with azetidine. Then that benzyl phenyl is attached to triazine via a bond formed later? Actually the triazine acyl chloride already includes that benzyl phenyl as substituent; the SN2 step is separate from acyl chloride formation. The acyl chloride is attached to triazine core; the benzyl phenyl is a substituent on triazine. So SN2 step yields the benzyl phenyl fragment, which is then part of the triazine acyl chloride (which is a separate molecule). But we can treat the triazine acyl chloride as having that fragment already; we can assume it's a building block that can be purchased or assembled separately. For simplicity, we can treat the triazine acyl chloride as a precursor that is commercially available (maybe). But we need three steps only; we already have amide formation and methoxy formation; the third step could be SN2 to make the benzyl phenyl fragment, but that fragment is part of the triazine acyl chloride, which we treat as product of SN2? Actually we can define the triazine acyl chloride as product of SN2 between chloromethyl phenyl and azetidine, then attached to triazine core via some other step not counted. This is messy.

Given constraints, we can present route with three reactions as described, even if chemically not perfect.

But note ordering: children of root are reactions? Usually each reaction node then its children are precursors. The order of reactions may be hierarchical: first reaction leads to target, its children are precursors which may themselves be molecules that have further children (reactions). So we need nested structure: target -> amide reaction -> anisidine (which is product of methoxy reaction) and triazine acyl chloride (product of SN2 reaction). So we need to nest: root children: one reaction (amide). That reaction children: two molecules: anisidine (type mol) and triazine acyl chloride (type mol). For anisidine, we add a child reaction (methoxy) that produces it from phenol and methyl carbonate. For triazine acyl chloride, we add child reaction (SN2) that produces it from chloromethyl phenyl and azetidine. So structure:
